newsitem.title: UK: BT offers to convert old plugs and sockets.
newsitem.headline: BT offers to convert old plugs and sockets.

text.p: British Telecommunications said on Monday it would convert old-style plugs and socket wiring free of charge over the next six months -- and would abolish the normal 29.38 stg fee permanently for "vulnerable" customers.

Those with impaired vision or hearing, a physical or mobility disability, who are chronically sick or have a progressive illness, will from today be able to buy or rent modern telephones with new accessories such as large buttons or loop hearing assistance, BT said in a statement.
Telecom watchdog Oftel welcomed the move that also allows people to choose who they buy a telephone from.

"I hope that all customers who have found the cost of conversion off-putting will take up this offer and, if they wish, take advantage of the wide variety of telecoms equipment available to buy in this very competitive part of the UK market," said Oftel deputy director general Anna Walker.
New plug and socket connections will also allow the elderly and disabled to join community alarm schemes.
BT said it would write to all customers who had "hardwired" telephones that are wired straight into walls. Alternatively, it noted, customers can telephone the company to ask for a free conversion.
